A 6.0 N weight hangs at the 10 cm mark on the left, and a 4.0 N weight hangs at the 80 cm mark on the right. (a) Calculate the distance of each weight from the 50 cm pivot. (b) Calculate the anticlockwise and clockwise moments and state which way the rule tips.
schoolQuestions.workedExample:
(a) Watch the trap! Always measure distance from the 50 cm PIVOT:
• Left weight (6.0 N at 10 cm mark): d₁ = 50 cm − 10 cm = 40 cm (0.40 m) from pivot.
• Right weight (4.0 N at 80 cm mark): d₂ = 80 cm − 50 cm = 30 cm (0.30 m) from pivot.
(b) Anticlockwise moment = 6.0 N × 40 cm = 240 N cm (2.4 N m).
Clockwise moment = 4.0 N × 30 cm = 120 N cm (1.2 N m).
Because the anticlockwise moment (240 N cm) is greater than the clockwise moment (120 N cm), the rule tips anticlockwise (left side goes down).
schoolQuestions.fadedPrompt: (a) Distances from the 50 cm pivot are d₁ = 50 − 10 = ________ cm and d₂ = 80 − 50 = ________ cm. (b) Anticlockwise moment = 6 × 40 = ________ N cm; clockwise moment = 4 × 30 = 120 N cm, so it tips ________.
schoolQuestions.modelAnswer: (a) Left distance from pivot = 50 − 10 = 40 cm; right distance = 80 − 50 = 30 cm. (b) Anticlockwise moment = 6.0 × 40 = 240 N cm; clockwise moment = 4.0 × 30 = 120 N cm. The rule tips anticlockwise (to the left).

schoolQuestions.bookSection: Workbook 6.6 Rocks in space & Unit 6 Check your progress (pp. 129–133)
schoolQuestions.prompt: Explain two reasons why the Moon's surface is covered in thousands of visible asteroid impact craters whereas Earth (which is right next to the Moon and has stronger gravity) has very few visible craters.
schoolQuestions.workedExample:
1. Atmosphere: Earth has a thick atmosphere; smaller asteroids (meteoroids) experience huge air resistance and friction as they enter Earth's atmosphere at high speed, heating up and burning away before hitting the ground. The Moon has no atmosphere.
2. Weathering, erosion & plate tectonics: On Earth, wind, rain, rivers, oceans, plant growth, and tectonic crust recycling erode or bury old craters over millions of years. The Moon has no liquid water, wind, or weather to erase craters.
schoolQuestions.fadedPrompt: 1. Earth's thick ________ burns up small asteroids by friction, whereas the Moon has no atmosphere. 2. On Earth, wind, water ________, and tectonic activity wear away old craters.
schoolQuestions.modelAnswer: 1. Earth has an atmosphere where air resistance/friction burns up most small rocks before impact, whereas the Moon has no atmosphere. 2. On Earth, weathering, erosion by water/wind, and geological activity wear away or cover craters over time.

callouts.hint: Least weight of water above this level

callouts.label: Bottom hole: greatest depth → highest pressure (P = ρgh) → farthest jet

diagramPlates.title: Law of Reflection in a Plane Mirror
diagramPlates.sourceRef: Learner's Book 8 · Topic 6.1 (p. 191) & Moving World Ch 10

callouts.label: Plane mirror (with hatching on non-reflective back)
callouts.hint: Flat reflecting surface

callouts.label: Normal (dashed line at 90° perpendicular to mirror)
callouts.hint: Reference line from which all optical angles are measured

callouts.label: Incident ray (with arrow pointing toward mirror, angle i)
callouts.hint: Incoming light ray from source

callouts.label: Reflected ray (with arrow leaving mirror, angle r = i)
callouts.hint: Outgoing light ray obeying angle of reflection = angle of incidence

diagramPlates.title: Refraction of Light Through a Rectangular Glass Block
diagramPlates.sourceRef: Learner's Book 8 · Topic 6.2 (p. 199) & Moving World Ch 10

callouts.label: Air → Glass: light slows down and bends TOWARD the normal (r < i)
callouts.hint: Entry boundary into optically denser medium

callouts.label: Refracted ray travelling slower inside the glass block
callouts.hint: Path through the transparent block

callouts.label: Glass → Air: light speeds up and bends AWAY from the normal
callouts.hint: Exit boundary into optically less dense air

callouts.label: Emergent ray (parallel to original incident ray)
callouts.hint: Final ray leaving parallel-sided block

diagramPlates.title: Dispersion of White Light by a Triangular Glass Prism
diagramPlates.sourceRef: Learner's Book 8 · Topic 6.3 (p. 205) & Moving World Ch 10

callouts.label: Incident narrow beam of white light (mixture of all wavelengths)
callouts.hint: Incoming polychromatic ray

callouts.label: Triangular glass prism (refracts light at both surfaces)
callouts.hint: Dispersive optical element

callouts.label: Red light (longest wavelength ~700 nm, slows least, refracted LEAST)
callouts.hint: Top band of the visible spectrum

callouts.label: Violet light (shortest wavelength ~400 nm, slows most, refracted MOST)
callouts.hint: Bottom band of the visible spectrum

diagramPlates.sourceRef: Learner's Book 8 · Topic 9.1 (p. 295) & Moving World Ch 13

callouts.label: North pole (field lines emerge outward; crowded = strong field)
callouts.hint: Arrows point away from this pole

callouts.hint: Arrows point toward this pole

callouts.label: Magnetic field line (continuous curve from N → S, never crosses)

callouts.label: Neutral point between repelling like poles (zero net magnetic field)

diagramPlates.title: Earth's Dipolar Magnetic Field & Outer Core Dynamo
diagramPlates.sourceRef: Learner's Book 8 · Topic 9.2 (p. 301) & Moving World Ch 13

callouts.label: Geographic North Pole (lies near a MAGNETIC SOUTH pole!)
callouts.hint: Field lines point inward here, attracting the N-tip of a compass

callouts.label: Convecting liquid iron & nickel outer core (generates the field)
callouts.hint: Geodynamo currents deep inside Earth

callouts.label: Geographic South Pole (lies near a magnetic north pole)
callouts.hint: Field lines emerge outward from the southern hemisphere

diagramPlates.title: Solenoid Electromagnet with Soft Iron Core & Ammeter Circuit
diagramPlates.sourceRef: Learner's Book 8 · Topics 9.3–9.4 (pp. 307–312) & Moving World Ch 13

callouts.label: Soft iron core (magnetises strongly with current, demagnetises when off)
callouts.hint: Temporary magnetic core inside the coil

callouts.label: Insulated wire coil / solenoid (more turns → stronger magnetic field)
callouts.hint: Current-carrying loops around the core

callouts.label: Ammeter in series (measures electric current I in amps)
callouts.hint: Instrument used to control or vary current accurately

callouts.label: Variable power supply & switch (switches magnetic field ON and OFF)
callouts.hint: Drives current round the circuit

diagramPlates.title: Earth's 23.4° Axial Tilt, Solstices & Lunar Phases
diagramPlates.sourceRef: The Moving World · Ch 14 (figs c14_seasons_tilt & c14_lunar_phases)

callouts.label: June solstice: Northern hemisphere tilted 23.4° toward Sun (higher solar altitude)
callouts.hint: Solar rays strike northern latitudes more directly (summer)

callouts.label: December solstice: Northern hemisphere tilted away from Sun (rays spread over larger area)
callouts.hint: Shorter daylight hours and lower solar angle in northern winter

callouts.label: Earth's spin axis stays pointed toward Polaris all year round
callouts.hint: Seasons are caused by axial tilt, NOT changing distance from the Sun!
